thread.title_full: 'I'll make her life hell': Warrant details texts before deadly Connecticut home invasion - NewsBreak

author: Jesse Leavenworth
title: 'I'll make her life hell': Warrant details texts before deadly Connecticut home invasion - NewsBreak
text:
By Jesse Leavenworth ,
8 hours ago Milford police at the scene of a fatal home invasion on June 3. Police say a man was killed and a woman wounded and two suspects were arrested. (Ethan Fry/Hearst Connecticut Media) MILFORD — A woman who was shot and wounded during a Milford home invasion that left her companion dead told police she thought immediately that the early morning attack was linked to an employee she had fired about a week before, an arrest warrant says.
Stuar Lopez-Reyes, 25, faces charges that include murder, assault on an elderly person and home invasion in the death of Frederick Werner, 69, and the wounding of Sandra Cooper on June 3 at their shorefront home. Cooper, also 69, survived a shot to the head and was able to call 911 after two men walked through an unlocked patio door into the couple's bedroom at around 2:50 a.m., police said. While she hid behind the bed, Werner was shot multiple times and later declared dead at the scene, the warrant says.
Police also arrested Ivan Barias-Florimon , 24, of the Bronx, N.Y., on charges that include murder and assault of an elderly victim.
Cooper told police that a former employee, a Bridgeport woman, was likely involved because Cooper had recently fired her on suspicion of stealing money from her real estate business, the warrant says. Police also traced a suspect vehicle, a Jeep Compass that was caught on surveillance cameras in the area, to the husband of the same woman, according to the warrant.
The Bridgeport woman told police she had worked for Cooper for three years before being fired on May 25, the warrant says. She told police she had been to Cooper's beachfront home several times and admitted her father-in-law normally drives the Jeep Compass, but noted that a man named Ivan, later identified as Barias-Florimon, who used to work for her husband's landscaping business, also had a key to the vehicle, the warrant says.
She also said her husband and Barias-Florimon had done work at Cooper's Milford home, the warrant says. Her husband told police that the last time he saw Barias-Florimon was on June 2 and assumed he was driving the Compass, the warrant said.
Barias-Florimon was hot-tempered and knew she had been fired, the woman said, according to police. He told her he never liked Cooper, saying "she had too much money for her own good," the warrant says. Asked by an investigator if Barias-Florimon "might feel like he had to stick up for her," the woman replied, "Of course I feel that way," the warrant says. Asked if he was capable of shooting someone, she said, "Yes, I'm sure," according to the warrant.
The woman also identified a second suspect from video footage as "Stu," before adding that he was "terrible" and that she was afraid of him, the warrant says. Stu was later identified as Lopez-Reyes, police said.
Texts between the woman and Barias-Florimon included his reaction to her being fired, according to the warrant.
"(Cooper) said she's going to make my life hell," the woman texted.
"I'll make her life hell," Barias-Florimon replied, according to the arrest warrant.
In a later exchange, Barias-Florimon texted, "Ouuuu (name of the Bridgeport woman) jus say the word I (expletive) her lifee OVE ," according to the warrant.
An autopsy found Werner suffered gunshot wounds to his head, chest, right thigh, pelvis, left buttock and right wrist, and the manner of his death was homicide, the warrant says.
On June 11, the state forensic laboratory reported that shell casings found at the crime scene matched a 9mm Glock pistol that New York City police seized on June 6, the warrant says. The gun had been stolen from Stratford in 2022, Milford police said.
Lopez-Reyes was being held on a $3 million bond for an appearance in state Superior Court in Milford on Sept. 10, according to court records. Barias-Florimon also was being held on a $3 million bond for a court appearance on Aug. 18, records show.
